turns.t: Good morning, everyone. Starting next week, the school will begin serving lunch in two shifts, because the cafeteria has become too crowded. Students in grades six and seven will eat at eleven thirty, and students in grades eight and nine will eat at twelve fifteen. Please check your schedule so that you go at the right time.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the announcement?
o: To explain a change in lunch times
questions.why: Lunch will be served in two shifts starting next week.

turns.t: Today we're going to practice finding the average of a set of numbers. First, add all the numbers together. Then count how many numbers there are. Finally, divide the total by that count. For example, if your test scores are eighty, ninety, and seventy, the total is two hundred forty, and two hundred forty divided by three equals eighty.

questions.q: What is the teacher explaining?
questions.why: She explains the steps for finding the average of numbers.

turns.t: For your homework, I'd like you to interview someone in your family about a childhood memory. Take notes during the interview, and then write one page about what you learned. Don't just copy what they say. Use your own words. We'll share the stories on Monday.

questions.q: What does the teacher want the students to do?
o: Write a story about a school trip
Interview a family member and write about it
Bring a family photo to class
questions.why: The homework is to interview a family member and write one page.

turns.t: Because of the heat, we're going to change today's class. Instead of running laps outside, we'll play volleyball in the gym. Please bring a water bottle and wear your sneakers. If anyone feels dizzy, sit down and tell me right away.

questions.q: Why is the class being changed?
questions.why: He says the class is changed 'because of the heat'.

turns.t: Many of you have asked how artists make colors look so bright. One trick is to place complementary colors next to each other. Complementary colors are opposites on the color wheel, such as red and green, or blue and orange. When you put them side by side, each color looks stronger. Try using this idea in your next painting.

questions.q: What will the students probably do next?
o: Paint a picture using opposite colors
Draw a color wheel for homework
questions.why: She tells them to use the idea of complementary colors in their next painting.

turns.t: The school newspaper is looking for new reporters. You don't need any experience, but you should enjoy writing and be curious about what happens at our school. We meet on Thursdays at lunch in Room 8. If you're interested, come to a meeting or talk to me after class.

questions.q: What does the speaker say about joining the newspaper?
o: Students should like writing and be curious
Students must be in ninth grade
questions.why: You don't need experience, but you should enjoy writing and be curious.

turns.t: Mr. Ortiz, do you have a minute?
Of course, Leo. What's up?
I haven't finished my poster for the science fair. I was home with the flu all last week.
I'm sorry to hear that. Are you feeling better?
Yes, much better. But I still need to add the graphs and the conclusion.
Well, the fair is on Friday, so I can't move that date. But I can give you until Wednesday afternoon to turn in the poster.
That would be great. Do I need a note from a doctor?
No, a note from your parents is enough. Just bring it with the poster.
Thanks. I'll stay after school tomorrow to finish the graphs.

questions.q: Why hasn't Leo finished his poster?
questions.why: He was home with the flu all last week.

questions.q: What does Mr. Ortiz agree to do?
o: Let Leo turn in the poster on Wednesday
questions.why: He can't move the fair, but gives Leo until Wednesday afternoon.

questions.q: What does Leo need to bring with the poster?
questions.why: A note from his parents is enough.

questions.q: What will Leo probably do tomorrow?
o: Stay after school to finish the graphs
questions.why: He says he'll stay after school tomorrow to finish the graphs.

turns.t: Have you decided on a topic for the history presentation?
Not yet. I was thinking about the pyramids, but I think half the class will choose that.
True. What about the Silk Road? We could talk about how people traded silk and spices.
That sounds interesting. Do we have enough information?
My aunt has a book about it, and I saw some good videos online.
Great. I'll write the script if you find the pictures.
Deal. Should we meet at the library on Thursday?
I have soccer practice on Thursday. How about Friday after lunch?
Friday works. I'll ask the teacher if we can use the computer room.

questions.q: Why does Daniel hesitate to choose the pyramids?
o: Many classmates will probably choose it
He has no information about it
questions.why: He thinks half the class will choose that topic.

questions.q: What topic do they decide on?
questions.why: Maya suggests the Silk Road and Daniel finds it interesting.

questions.q: What will Maya do for the project?
o: Bring a book from the library
questions.why: Daniel will write the script if Maya finds the pictures.

questions.q: When will they meet?
questions.why: Daniel has soccer on Thursday, so they agree on Friday after lunch.

turns.t: Today we're going to talk about the water cycle, which is the path water takes as it moves around our planet. The cycle begins when the sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. Some of this water changes into a gas called water vapor and rises into the air. This process is called evaporation. As the vapor rises, the air gets colder, and the vapor turns back into tiny drops of liquid water. This is called condensation, and it's how clouds are formed. When the drops in a cloud become heavy enough, they fall to the ground as rain, snow, or hail. Scientists call this precipitation. Finally, some of the water flows into rivers and returns to the ocean, and the cycle begins again.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the talk?
o: How water moves around the Earth
questions.why: She describes the path water takes around the planet.

questions.q: What causes evaporation?
questions.why: The sun heats water, and some becomes water vapor.

questions.q: What happens during condensation?
o: Water vapor turns into tiny drops of liquid
questions.why: The vapor turns back into tiny drops of liquid water, forming clouds.

questions.q: What is precipitation?
o: Water falling from clouds to the ground
questions.why: Drops fall as rain, snow, or hail, which is called precipitation.

turns.t: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly, and most of them are active at night. This raises an interesting question: how can a bat find food in complete darkness? The answer is echolocation. A bat makes high-pitched sounds, too high for humans to hear, as it flies. These sounds travel through the air until they hit an object, such as an insect, and then bounce back to the bat as echoes. The bat's ears are very sensitive, and its brain uses the echoes to figure out the size, shape, and distance of the object. Some bats can find an insect smaller than a mosquito this way. Echolocation is so accurate that a bat can fly through a dark room full of thin wires without touching one. Engineers have used the same idea to build sonar, which helps ships find objects underwater.

questions.q: Why does the speaker ask how a bat finds food in the dark?
o: To introduce the topic of echolocation
To show that bats cannot see
To explain why bats are mammals
questions.why: The question leads to the answer: echolocation.

questions.q: What is echolocation?
o: Using echoes of sounds to find objects
questions.why: Bats send out sounds and use the echoes that bounce back.

questions.q: What can a bat learn from an echo?
o: The color and taste of an object
The size, shape, and distance of an object
questions.why: The brain uses echoes to figure out size, shape, and distance.

questions.q: What can be inferred about the sounds bats make?
o: They are very loud to humans
They are the same as human voices
questions.why: The sounds are too high for humans to hear.

questions.q: What does the speaker say about sonar?
o: Engineers used the same idea to build it
questions.why: Engineers used the same idea to build sonar for finding objects underwater.
